einzeiler: Cellular health, lifestyle choices, and reconnecting with faith to reverse aging.
kurzfassung: Experts Dr. Josh Axe and Dr. Will Cole join a roundtable discussion on the cutting-edge science of cellular health and the importance of reversing organ aging. They explore how simple lifestyle factors like sleep, nutrition, and stress management deeply impact metabolic and cellular function. Additionally, they highlight how spiritual well-being and a connection with faith can significantly lower inflammation and improve overall longevity.
stichpunkte: One in five people have an organ aging faster than the rest of the body, significantly increasing mortality risk.
Cellular dysfunction is the root cause of chronic illness, surpassing traditional mainstream views focused solely on downstream organ disease.
Poor sleep and disrupted circadian rhythms directly spike insulin resistance and chronic inflammation.
High cortisol and insulin are primary drivers of hormonal imbalance and can be managed through lifestyle and vagal nerve toning.
Bio-individuality matters in nutrition, meaning extreme diets like strict carnivore or veganism are rarely suitable as permanent lifestyles for everyone.
Faith practices, spiritual connection, and reduced childhood trauma are statistically linked to lower inflammation and increased longevity.
Therapeutic peptides hold significant potential for healing and recovery, though the market suffers from regulation issues and low-quality black-market products.
Building muscle mass through safe weight training is vital for improving mitochondrial density and supporting metabolic health as we age.

clips.hook: One in five people have an organ aging faster than the body
clips.text: A Stanford study discovered that twenty percent of individuals experience accelerated aging in a single specific organ, which heavily raises the risk of severe medical emergencies in that area.

clips.hook: Strengthening the vagus nerve for better sleep and recovery
clips.text: The vagus nerve functions like a muscle that requires active and passive conditioning to improve resting states, digestion, and deep sleep quality.

clips.hook: Faith practices reduce mortality risk by 33 percent
clips.text: Harvard research indicates that maintaining a regular faith practice and community connection correlates with a substantial decrease in all-cause mortality over a sixteen-year span.

beschreibung:
Welcome to my special 175th EPISODE!

This is also my very first special roundtable interview! I could not have had two better than Dr. Josh Axe and Dr. Will Cole as my first guests! These roundtables are a gathering of the most brilliant and impactful minds, coming together to offer deep thoughts and insights of the most discussed aspects of health, wellness and faith! These roundtables will be continuing as special episodes each month to continue to do God's work in bringing as many of us together to make the biggest impact possible!! ENJOY!!

For years, I thought that if I ate right, trained hard, stayed disciplined, and took care of my body, I was doing everything I needed to stay healthy.

But I've learned that being healthy on the outside doesn't always mean everything is healthy on the inside.

My father passed away from a heart attack at just 59 years old. And despite everything I've done to take care of myself, I recently discovered that I have elevated Lp(a) levels and plaque in my arteries.

That was a wake-up call.

It made me realize just how much can be happening inside our bodies without us ever knowing it.

That's why this conversation with Dr. Josh Axe and Dr. Will Cole was so important to me.

Dr. Josh Axe and Dr. Will Cole are leading voices in functional medicine, bestselling authors, and longtime advocates for looking beyond symptoms to understand the underlying factors affecting our health.

Together, they've written Heal Your Cells, a book exploring how cellular health, inflammation, metabolism, and lifestyle may influence chronic disease and the aging process.

We talked about how our organs can age faster than our bodies, the hidden risks of heart disease, and how stress and trauma affect our health.

One of the most meaningful parts for me was discussing faith and how true health goes beyond the physical. It's about caring for our minds, bodies, and our relationship with God.

And it made me wonder:

What if the biggest threats to our health are the things we can't see or feel until it's too late?

In This Episode, We Talk About:

■ Cellular health, mitochondria, and chronic disease

■ The blood markers that may reveal problems before symptoms appear

■ Insulin resistance, inflammation, and metabolic health

■ How stress, childhood trauma, and the nervous system affect the body

■ The connection between faith, emotional healing, and physical health

■ Gut health, exercise, and the importance of personalized nutrition

■ Why looking healthy doesn't always mean being healthy
